FIXED 2026-11-24. Twenty consecutive runs of the file pass, against roughly five failures in twelve before; three consecutive full-workspace runs are clean.

## The first diagnosis was wrong, which is the useful part

The intuitive explanation -- CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR persists, the scripts had fixed names, so a run truncates a script a lingering process from the previous run is still executing -- is wrong. It is plausible: ETXTBSY really is what Linux returns when you open-for-write a file being executed, the directory really does persist, and the scripts really do background long sleeps.

It was tested and disproved. Giving each process its own scratch directory AND staging every write to a sibling path then renaming it into place changed nothing: five of twelve runs still failed. Renaming cannot hit ETXTBSY at all, since it swaps a directory entry without touching the inode, so the failure had to be somewhere else.

## The actual cause

The error surfaces at exec, not at write. ETXTBSY on execve means some descriptor somewhere has the file open for writing, and the harness runs these four tests concurrently:

1. a thread writing a script holds a write descriptor on it;
2. another thread spawning a child calls fork, and the child inherits a duplicate of every descriptor the parent holds, including that one;
3. execve in the child refuses with ETXTBSY while that duplicate exists.

So the write and the exec never need to touch the same file. One test writing its own script is enough to break a different test's spawn, which is why a different test failed each time and why per-process paths were irrelevant -- the descriptor is the problem, not the path.

## The fix

All four scripts are written inside a single LazyLock. Whichever test reaches it first performs every write while the others block on the lock; once it releases, no write descriptor is open again for the remainder of the run. Tests still run in parallel.

LazyLock is Rust 1.80, so this fix was not available at the old MSRV of 1.73 and is one of the things the bump to 1.88 unlocked.

## Other sites, as this bead asked

pkix-policy-zlint/tests/review_intern.rs has the same write-then-spawn shape. It is safe, but only because it contains exactly one test, so there is no second thread to be forking during its write. That is incidental rather than structural, so it now carries a comment saying exactly that and pointing at this fix -- adding a second test to that file reintroduces the race.

No other test in the workspace writes an executable and then runs it. Checked by grepping for set_permissions and from_mode across all crates.

## Acceptance

[x] The executable is closed before being spawned -- achieved by ordering all writes ahead of all spawns, which is the property that actually matters; closing the handle was never the issue, since std::fs::write already does that
[x] The file passes repeated full-workspace runs -- twenty runs of the file and three full-workspace runs, against an observed rate of roughly one failure in two
[x] Other write-then-exec tests checked -- one found, documented rather than changed, with the reason it is currently safe
